page: Microsoft Azure FX8-4mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with a high base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 vCPUs, which are derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, and a massive 168.0 GB of RAM. This configuration translates to an exceptional 42.0 GB of memory per core. It includes 472 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage, but does not bundle any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The high 4.2 GHz clock speed drives top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2355.0 and strong single-threaded compression metrics, including 34.91 GB/sec for Gzip and 14.41 GB/sec for Bzip3. However, due to the low core count, multi-core performance is relatively weak, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 4441.77 and a weak multi-threaded Bzip3 decompression rate of 28.72 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth also shows a performance drop from cached small-block reads at 344.91 GB/sec to uncached large-block reads at 36.17 GB/sec.

This hardware profile is highly specialized for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, and text processing tasks. Conversely, it is poorly suited for parallelized compilation, multi-threaded high-performance computing, or large-scale LLM inference. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density for memory-heavy applications, allowing users to avoid paying for unneeded vCPUs just to acquire a large memory footprint, though the low core count remains a clear tradeoff for compute-heavy tasks.
